import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1007

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1007](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1007)
- [ChNo16] Chaffee, Joe and Noble, Matt, *Dimension 4 and dimension 5 graphs with minimum edge
  set*. Australas. J. Combin. (2016), 327-333.
- [Ho13] House, Roger F., *A 4-dimensional graph has at least 9 edges*. Discrete Math. (2013),
  1783-1789.
-/

namespace Erdos1007

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

variable {V : Type*}

/-- The complete tripartite graph $K_{1,3,3}$. -/
abbrev K133 := SimpleGraph.completeMultipartiteGraph fun i : Fin 3 => Fin (![1, 3, 3] i)

/--
The dimension of a graph $G$ is the minimal $n$ such that $G$ can be embedded in $\mathbb{R}^n$
such that every edge of $G$ is a unit line segment.

What is the smallest number of edges in a graph with dimension $4$?

Answer: The smallest number of edges is $9$, achieved solely by $K_{3,3}$, proved by House [Ho13]. An
alternative proof was given by Chaffee and Noble [ChNo16], who also prove that the smallest
number of edges in a graph of dimension $5$ is $15$ (achieved by $K_6$ and $K_{1,3,3}$).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1007.lean"]
theorem erdos_1007 :
    IsLeast {m | ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G.HasDimension 4 ∧ G.edgeSet.ncard = m}
      9 := by
  sorry

/--
The smallest number of edges in a graph of dimension $4$ is achieved solely by $K_{3,3}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_1007.variants.dimension_four_extremal (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (hdim : G.HasDimension 4) (hcard : G.edgeSet.ncard = 9)
    (hdeg : ∀ v : Fin n, ∃ w : Fin n, G.Adj v w) :
    Nonempty (G ≃g completeBipartiteGraph (Fin 3) (Fin 3)) := by
  sorry

/--
The smallest number of edges in a graph of dimension $5$ is $15$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_1007.variants.dimension_five :
    IsLeast {m | ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G.HasDimension 5 ∧ G.edgeSet.ncard = m}
      15 := by
  sorry

/--
The smallest number of edges in a graph of dimension $5$ is achieved by $K_6$ and $K_{1,3,3}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_1007.variants.dimension_five_extremal :
    ((SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 6)).HasDimension 5 ∧
        (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 6)).edgeSet.ncard = 15) ∧
      (K133.HasDimension 5 ∧ K133.edgeSet.ncard = 15) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1007

reformulations.difference: The hypothesis hdeg explicitly excludes isolated vertices, making precise the source's shorthand that the minimum is achieved 'solely by K_{3,3}'.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Uniqueness must be understood modulo isolated vertices. For a finite graph with nine edges, deleting isolated vertices preserves the edge count and dimension: representations restrict to the support, and in every positive dimension they extend by placing the finitely many isolated vertices outside the existing image. Dimension zero is impossible because an edge remains. The theorem restricted to graphs without isolated vertices is therefore equivalent to asserting, for every dimension-four nine-edge graph G, that G.induce G.support is isomorphic to K_{3,3}. This exact equivalence was proved as uniqueness_modulo_isolates_iff in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, without using the problem's sorry theorems.

reformulations.difference: The linked formal proof quantifies over arbitrary finite vertex types, defines dimension using sInf, and counts edges with edgeFinset.card. The repository uses Fin n, HasDimension, and edgeSet.ncard.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite vertex type can be relabelled as Fin n; graph isomorphisms preserve unit-distance embeddability and edge counts. For finite edge sets, ncard equals edgeFinset.card. Moreover, sInf of the set of admissible dimensions equals 4 exactly when 4 is its least element: the empty-set default is zero, so it cannot introduce a spurious dimension-four graph. The complete linked theorem statement was proved equivalent to the repository statement as linked_statement_iff in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, with only standard Lean axioms.

review.notes: Checked K133 and all four theorems. The paper explicitly uses finite simple graphs and does not require nonadjacent vertices to have distance different from one, matching the Lean definition. Lean checks verified the edge counts 9, 15, and 15, K133's seven vertices, and empty/singleton boundary cases. Both scratch files compile, and the equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies. The current source-linked database records 'solved (Lean)', consistent with the metadata. Access limitations: the live Erdős page and House's full text were blocked; the archived page and Chaffee–Noble's full paper cover every mathematical claim. The linked proof contains no sorry or custom axioms by inspection, but its original Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1 build was not reproduced in the 4.33.1 sandbox; its statement equivalence was independently kernel-checked.
